positions.name: GateMandateRationale
positions.frame: what past failure does the signed-manifest requirement respond to, and how does that history license the mandate?
positions.why: src-1 issues the binding requirement as a command performative ('now requires... before it ships'), while src-2 supplies the evidentiary basis in plain, activated-negative register ('two unsigned artifacts reach staging... the whole reason for the gate'). Read together, the pair moves from cause to consequence — a directive backed by rational-persuasion rather than authority alone (power dimension marks src-2 as rational-persuasion, distinct from the legitimate-power mint on the surrounding fields). The tension is genuine: src-1 enacts without argument, src-2 argues without enacting; the frame holds both as one justificatory arc.

positions.name: GateFormalRecord
positions.frame: how does the gate decision get formalized into discrete, owned, accountable fields rather than narrated as prose?
positions.why: src-3, src-4, and src-5 share a single structural pattern — bolded label followed by a compressed clause (Gate/Scope/Owner) — noted across style (short-punchy-cadence run), register (technical lexis, and the labeled-field-accountability mint anchored on src-5), and relational/power dimensions (authority-ranking, legitimate power, all three carrying the same mint verdicts). Together they convert the directive of src-1 into a standing record: what the rule is, where it binds, who answers for it. This is a distinct directional read from the prose justification in GateMandateRationale — the same decision rendered as institutional record rather than narrated cause-and-effect.
